_comment: SP-066: the image pick's rubric, read by lib/pick.js (Jev), shaped like scripts/story-rubric.json's axes. One Score question per scored cell and axis; Jev answers a level 0-2, and the axis score is that + 1 (decimals kept, as US-038 keeps them). An axis's optional "check" is added to its question. SP-066 changes SP-064's rubric so that vivid scores the scene (what the story objects do to each other), not the camera, with the angle exception of C-042 (ADR-0033). After stage 5 (ADR-0037), must-see clarity has no levels of its own: it is scored in parts (C-046), one Score question per scored cell and part, each with its own levels and check (the clarity check comes first), and clarity is the mean of the parts that apply: completeness, size and state always, nameSign only for a name anchor, view only when the story has a main subject (C-045). Code caps no score: Jev sees the drawing errors when it scores plausible, and name_sign_readable when it scores the name sign.

plausible.label: Plausible
levels: the scene makes little sense: no setting clues, or the action happens in an order that doesn't fit the story
the scene makes some sense: a few setting clues, or a mostly sensible order of action
the scene makes sense: clear setting clues such as a floor, a hand or a height, and a sensible order of action
plausible.check: A drawing error (an object in the cell's drawing_errors: it floats, looks pasted on, or breaks the lines of the wall or floor) makes the scene make less sense, so give the cell a lower score for it: one on a must-see item costs more than one on another object.

vivid.label: Vivid
vivid.check: Score the scene, not the camera: what the story objects do to each other, from the cell's action line and the sizes of its must-see items. An eye-level, medium shot is the normal view, and an extreme close-up or a strong camera angle adds nothing. An unusual camera angle lowers vivid only when it hides the action; an unusual angle never lowers vivid when the state's angle_case is "view" (the story is about a view) or "one-object" (the story has one main object).
levels: the story objects are small, far away or apart from each other
the story objects are clear, but they don't act on each other as the story says
the story objects are large and act on each other as the story says

clarity.label: Must-see clarity
clarity.check: Must-see clarity is scored in parts, one question each; this question scores one part only, from the cell's full description. A name sign is not a must-see item.

completeness.label: Must-see clarity: completeness
completeness.check: Use each must-see item's mark (visible / partly cut / hidden) and the cell's shot. A crop that fits the shot, as when a close-up cuts the edge of an item, costs less than a crop that cuts off part of the story (the hand that acts, the thing it acts on).
levels: a crop cuts off part of the story: a must-see item that the story needs is partly cut off by the edge of the picture
a must-see item is partly cut, but the crop fits the shot (as in a close-up)
every must-see item is fully visible

size.label: Must-see clarity: size
size.check: Use each must-see item's size (large / medium / small). An item that is small by nature, such as a headlamp or a ring, costs less than a story item drawn too small to see what it does.
levels: a story item is too small to see what it does
an item is small by nature (such as a headlamp), and every other must-see item is large enough to see
every must-see item is large enough to see

state.label: Must-see clarity: state
state.check: Check each must-see item with its adjectives: the item must be shown in the state its adjectives give (a bare cob). The cell's must-see marks say only whether an item is there, not its state: use the cell's objects and their adjectives.
levels: a must-see item is not in the state its adjectives give (a cob that isn't bare yet)
the state of some must-see items is unclear
every must-see item is in the state its adjectives give

nameSign.label: Must-see clarity: name sign
nameSign.check: Use the cell's readable text (extras.readableText) and its name_sign_readable: can every name sign (name_signs) be read on the item that carries it, such as "Venice" on the nurse's nametag?
levels: a name sign can't be read (no "Venice" on the nurse's nametag)
a name sign is partly readable or misread
every name sign can be read

view.label: Must-see clarity: main-subject view
view.check: Use the cell's main_view, the view of the story's main subject (main_subject): where its face and body point. When main_view is null (the main subject is hidden), give the lowest level.
levels: the main subject is seen from the back or from above, or is hidden
the main subject is seen from the side
the main subject is seen from the front or in three-quarter view
